english.title: Record image of another while breast-feeding a child
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without reasonably believing that she consented, recorded an image of her while she was breast feeding a child with the intention that you or a third person would look at the image for the purpose of obtaining sexual gratification for yourself or that other person, or to humiliate, alarm or distress her
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 67A(2B) and (4) of the Sexual Offences Act 2003.

investigatoraction.description: Attracts liability for entry on sex offenders register

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) A reference to breast-feeding a child includes re-arranging clothing, see section 67A(3A).
(ii) It is irrelevant whether the person breast-feeding is in a public place or not, and whether or not the person's breasts are exposed while breast-feeding and what part of the person's body is, or is intended to be visible in the recorded image, see section 67A(3A).
(iii) As per section 67A(3)(a) if the offence is being committed for sexual gratification, the gratification can be for the person recording the offence or for other persons.
(iv) See further paragraphs 29 to 34 of Home Office Circular 005/2022.
(v) Victims of this offence are entitled to anonymity under section 2 of the Sexual Offences (Amendment) Act 1992.

other.penalty:
Either way

Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Note
The maximum penalty on summary conviction may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020
